title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies a deterministic validator and at most one deterministic rule-based repair to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success relative to ungated LLM generation. Generation used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per intent; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator when eligibility rules were met. Primary outcomes (artifact-backed): baseline = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We describe the deterministic validator and repair operator used, provide execution-accounting totals (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1), clarify the exact statistical test implementation appropriate for small discordant counts, and archive all prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: LLM-driven NetOps workflows (intent→configuration) promise to reduce human operator effort but raise operational-safety concerns: configurations must be syntactically correct, preserve protected state, satisfy ordering/dependency constraints (e.g., make-before-break), and produce the intended final control-plane state when executed. Prior prototypes and surveys report structured-output failures and propose mitigations—RAG, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and tool-augmented pipelines—but comparative, execution-grounded evidence of the marginal utility of bounded deterministic repairs applied to the same initial LLM candidate remains limited. We therefore preregistered a narrowly scoped paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates low-cost repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness by sharing a single initial candidate across baseline (ungated) and guarded (validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) arms. Our research question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms evaluate the same initial candidate? Contributions: (1) an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired evaluation under a shared-candidate estimand with complete artifact archiving; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic 3-stage validator and the deterministic repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) exact-test selection and execution accounting appropriate for small discordant counts and low per-intent model-call budgets.
sections.related_work: LLMs have been applied to intent-driven configuration, intent translation, and co-pilot tasks for network management in academic and prototype systems; these efforts demonstrate feasibility but vary in execution grounding and deployment realism [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]. Cross-domain mitigation approaches (RAG, live schema grounding, constrained decoding) reduce hallucinations in structured-output tasks (e.g., NL2SQL) and motivate verifier-augmented NetOps architectures [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6909831]. Formal verification frameworks and NetKAT variants provide deterministic checks for reachability and policy properties and are natural validators for generated configs, though fidelity and scalability trade-offs remain [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Recent architectural analyses emphasize assurance machinery (audit traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) around agentic NetOps rather than relying on LLM outputs alone [https://openalex.org/W7161165783]. Our study complements this literature by experimentally measuring the marginal return of a low-cost deterministic repair applied directly to a single shared candidate, an operationally relevant estimand when minimizing hosted-model calls is a priority.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) defines a paired, shared-initial-generation estimand over n=200 curated natural-language intents that target small single- and multi-device configuration changes (VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns, safe-sequence policies). For each intent a single hosted-model generation served both arms: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validation + ≤1 deterministic repair when eligible). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the preregistered primary test is McNemar’s paired binary test implemented in exact-binomial form appropriate for small discordant totals. The planned model-call budget was 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls recorded = 1). The confirmatory environment used containerized Mininet+FRR routers and a deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement before the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. 

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"); execution used a hosted-model interface recorded in the execution manifest. Model configuration recorded: max_output_tokens = 2000, provider = openai_responses, requested_model = gpt-5-mini. Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. The deterministic repair operator is rule-based and invoked without additional LLM calls. The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); paired-bootstrap CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle rather than enumerated inline to preserve concise manuscript presentation.
